biggest_catch: This is only for customers who already participated in a Duke income-qualified program (Neighborhood Energy Saver, Weatherization, or the High Energy Use pilot) in the last 36 months — prior participation is the gate.
catches: You must have participated in Duke Energy Neighborhood Energy Saver, Weatherization, or the High Energy Use pilot within the last 36 months.
Residential electric service in your name; you must occupy the enrolled residence.
Centrally ducted electric air conditioning and/or heating required (window units do not qualify); home Wi-Fi and an active email required.
Renters need the Tenant Authorization Form plus landlord/property-owner approval.
Duke installs the equipment for free and adjusts enrolled appliances a few times per month during peak demand.
No fee; the thermostat (if you don't have one) is installed free.

steps: Confirm you participated in Duke Energy Neighborhood Energy Saver, Weatherization, or the High Energy Use pilot in the last 36 months.
Check you have centrally ducted electric AC/heating, home Wi-Fi, and an active email (renters: get landlord approval via the Tenant Authorization Form).
Enroll in Power Manager on the official Duke Energy page (or call 866-541-8886 for help).
Let Duke install the free smart thermostat (or enroll your existing eligible device).
Receive $150 off your next bill, plus $50 off annually while you stay enrolled.
timing: $150 off your next bill after enrollment, plus $50 off annually while enrolled.
